message:
## Provisional design: 768 compounds/day two-stage combinatorial library with QC and fluorescence screen

**No tools were available.** I could not search the catalog, retrieve evidence, simulate or verify. Every throughput statement below is my own model-based prediction and has not been simulated. Nothing here is measured lab performance.

### Assumptions I had to make
I could not ask follow-up questions, so these are mine. Please correct them.
- **Throughput:** 768 compounds/day as an operating target. Combinatorial arithmetic: 8 row building blocks x 12 column building blocks x 8 blocks/day = 768. That is 96 products per 96-well reaction block, so 8 blocks/day.
- **Operating hours:** 24 h/day automated. Operators work 3 x 8 h shifts: 3 chemists and 3 lab technicians, one of each per shift.
- **Room:** assumed 15 m x 10 m x 3 m, with one door at (0, 5). There is no layout engine, so no coordinates or placement check exist.
- **Budget:** none given. This is a **provisional** design. The catalog BOM is about **$3.34 M**, excluding staff, installation, building exhaust and consumables.
- **Hazards:** flammable solvents and toxic reagents are assumed. Inert atmosphere was not requested. The SWING XL supports it if needed.
- **What "compounds" means:** one compound is one well that is synthesised, QC'd and screened. Synthesis success and purity yield are unknown. The count is attempted products that pass through QC and screening, not QC-passed compounds.

### Flow (flow unit: one 96-well reaction block, later one 96-well library/assay plate; all durations per block run, batch_size 1, fan_out 1)
| Step | Instance(s) | Duration per block | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Load block from hotel | hotel_1 | 0 s | — |
| Operator replenishment (vials, tips, solvent reservoirs, labels) | bench_1, chemist | 900 s | catalog lab_bench (placeholder) |
| Stock preparation (powder dosing) | quantos_1, chemist attends | 300 s | catalog (estimated per-run; likely optimistic) |
| Stage-1 building-block distribution | biomek_1 | 600 s | catalog |
| **Reaction stage 1** | reactor_1–4 (shared pool) | 14 400 s | catalog SWING XL |
| Workup / filtration | biotage_1, chemist | 300 s | catalog |
| Stage-2 addition | biomek_1 | 600 s | catalog |
| **Reaction stage 2** | reactor_1–4 (shared pool) | 14 400 s | catalog |
| Purification (SPE) | biotage_1, chemist | 600 s | catalog |
| Evaporation | evap_1 (EZ-2, 4 slots) | 5 400 s | catalog |
| Reformat / redissolve to library plate | biomek_1 | 600 s | catalog |
| **LC-MS QC, 96 samples/plate** | lcms_1, lcms_2 | 14 400 s per plate | catalog value; I read it as already plate-level (96 x ~150 s/sample) |
| Stamp assay plate from library plate | biomek_1 | 600 s | catalog |
| Archive library mother plate in −80 °C | freezer_1, lab_technician | 120 s handling | agent estimate |
| Assay reagent dispense | multidrop_1 | 10 s (+60 s setup) | catalog datasheet |
| Incubation | incubator_1 (Cytomat, 42 slots) | 3 600 s residence | catalog |
| Fluorescence read | reader_1 | 180 s | catalog |
| Hit analysis (**counting sink**, 96 compounds per plate) | in silico | 600 s | agent estimate |

**Transport:**
- kmr_1, a KUKA KMR iiwa mobile manipulator, handles inter-cell moves.
- ur5e_1 serves the screening cell (Multidrop, Cytomat, reader).
- Chemists move blocks into and out of the Biotage manifold.

### Capacity arithmetic (optimistic per-step bounds, not throughput proof)
- **Reactors:** each block needs 2 x 14 400 = 28 800 s of reactor time. For 8 blocks that is 230 400 s/day. One reactor-day is 86 400 s, so at least 3 reactors are needed. I used **4** (345 600 s/day, ~67% utilisation, ceiling ~12 blocks/day).
  - At the high-end assumption of 18 000 s per reaction, 4 reactors still give ~9.6 blocks/day.
  - With 3 reactors, utilisation would be 89% and the margin would be too thin.
- **LC-MS:** 8 x 14 400 = 115 200 s/day, which exceeds one instrument, so 2 are needed (~67%, ceiling ~12 blocks/day).
- **Biomek 4000:** 4 steps x 600 s x 8 = 19 200 s/day (22%).
- **Biotage:** about 7 200 s/day plus setup.
- **Chemist-attended time:** about 2 100 s per block, or ~4.7 h/day spread across 3 shifts.
- **Likely bottleneck:** the reactor pool and the LC-MS pair are co-limiting at about 12 blocks/day, i.e. ~1 150 compounds/day theoretical.
  - I predict a p50 of about 960 compounds/day after transfers and variability.
  - Confidence that p50 ≥ 768 is about 0.65.

**Simulation settings:** a single block takes about 16 h end to end before transfers. I recommend a horizon of at least 7 days with a 2-day warm-up excluded. A 1-day horizon would badly undercount throughput.

### Gaps and disclosures
- **Compound storage:** the only catalog compound store costs $3.16 M, so I left it out. The library is archived in a −80 °C freezer by a technician instead. If you need automated compound storage, I can add it.
- **Solvent storage:** the Justrite cabinet is catalogued only as `waste`. I use it for flammable solvent and waste segregation; check that this matches your site's requirements.
- **Ventilation:**
  - Filtration, SPE and the evaporator exhaust are in fume hoods.
  - The SWING XL reactors and the LC-MS need ducted extraction. That is facility work, not a catalog item.
  - None of this is safety certification.
- **Cheaper reactor option:** the Chemspeed ISYNTH ($500 k, **placeholder** price, no inert atmosphere) could save about $377 k. It has the same 14 400 s reaction time.
- **Quantos timing:** the 300 s per-run figure is a catalog estimate. Weighing 20+ building blocks per block may take longer, which would load the chemists more.
- **Library-archive step:** it is in line in the model. Physically, the mother plate goes to the freezer while the assay plate continues.
- **Evidence:** all durations come from catalog fields or are labelled agent_estimate. No literature was retrieved.

### Claims to verify
- p50 ≥ 768 compounds/day.
- BOM ≈ $3.34 M; no budget was given, so this cannot be checked against one.
- Zero layout violations; low confidence, because nothing was placed.

lab_spec.name: 768 compounds/day combinatorial library synthesis, QC and screening lab
lab_spec.description: Design a 768-compound/day combinatorial library and screening lab. Agent assumptions (not user-confirmed): two-stage synthesis in 96-well reaction blocks (8 x 12 x 8 = 768 products/day = 8 blocks/day), LC-MS QC of every product, fluorescence screening readout, 24 h operation, provisional budget.
notes: Budget not provided: provisional design, catalog BOM ~3.34M USD.
Room dimensions, operating hours and hazards assumed by agent; operators are 3 x 8 h shifts (one chemist and one technician per shift).
Throughput counts attempted products that are QC'd and screened; synthesis/QC pass yield unknown.
Compound storage via -80 C freezer with manual archiving; automated compound store omitted on cost.
Reactors and LC-MS require site exhaust ducting not represented in catalog.
Recommended simulation: >=7-day horizon, 2-day warm-up; single-block latency ~16 h.

claims.statement: Predicted p50 throughput is about 960 compounds/day (>= 768 target) in steady state; reactor pool and LC-MS pair co-limit near ~1150/day. Prediction only, not simulated or measured.
Catalog BOM total is about 3,343,836 USD (operators, installation, exhaust and consumables excluded); no budget was supplied.
Equipment fits the assumed 15 m x 10 m room with no layout violations (not placed or checked).
